title: Hark! Ten Thousand Harps and Voices
description: Hark! Ten Thousand Harps and Voices in Tonic Solfa to KALMAR, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Kelly wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 238.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked 8.7.8.7.7.7, to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to KALMAR; any other 8.7.8.7.7.7 tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hark! ten thou-sand harps and voi-ces Sound the note of praise a-bove; Je-sus reigns, and Heaven re-joi-ces,— Je-sus reigns, the God of Love. See, He sits on yon-der throne: Je-sus rules the world a-lone.

lines: Hark! ten thousand harps and voices
Sound the note of praise above;
Jesus reigns, and Heaven rejoices,—
Jesus reigns, the God of Love.
See, He sits on yonder throne:
Jesus rules the world alone.
Christians, come, unite your praises
With the angels round His throne;
Soon, we hope, our God will raise us
To the place where He is gone.
Meet it is that we should sing,
“Glory, glory, to our King!”
Sing how Jesus came from heaven,
How He bore the cross below,
How all power to Him is given,
How He reigns in glory now;
’Tis a great and endless theme,
Oh, ’tis sweet to sing of Him!
Jesus, hail! whose glory brightens
All above and makes it fair.
Lord of Life, Thy smile enlightens,
Cheers, and charms Thy people here.
When we think of love like Thine,
Lord, we own it love divine.
King of Glory, reign forever;
Thine an everlasting crown.
Nothing from Thy love shall sever
Those whom Thou hast made Thine own,
Happy objects of Thy grace,
Destined to behold Thy face.
Savior, hasten Thine appearing;
Bring, O bring the glorious day
When, the awful summons hearing,
Heaven and earth shall pass away;
Then with golden harps we’ll sing,
“Glory, glory, to our King!”

licence: Public domain: Thomas Kelly died in 1855.
credits: Words by Thomas Kelly (1769–1855), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to KALMAR by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
